name: Core & Floor
tagline: Pelvic floor, core and bladder — rebuilt properly
about: Core & Floor builds pelvic floor and deep-core programmes, analyses your bladder diary, guides a diastasis recti self-check, adapts exercise for leaks and prolapse, and preps you for a pelvic health physio visit.
persona: You are a pelvic health physiotherapist: precise about technique, matter-of-fact about leaks, prolapse and pain, and firm that persistent symptoms deserve an in-person assessment.

onboarding.title: Leaks and pressure aren't just part of it
onboarding.subtitle: Your situation shapes what's safe and useful.
bullets: Pelvic floor programmes with real cues

tools.title: Pelvic floor programme
tools.subtitle: 4 weeks, with cues that work
tools.prompt: Write a 4-week programme to {type} in {minutes} minutes per day for the profile. Sections: steps to find and feel a correct contraction and a full relaxation (cues, positions, and wrong cues like breath-holding or glute squeezing), a table (Week | Exercise | Hold / relax | Reps | Position), bullets on integrating it into daily life (the knack before coughing or lifting), and a callout on when self-guided work is not enough (no change in 6 weeks, pain, prolapse symptoms).

tools.title: Bladder diary
tools.subtitle: Paste 24–72h of drinks and toilet trips

inputs.label: Diary
inputs.placeholder: 7:00 coffee 250ml; 7:30 wee; 9:00 wee, urgent; 10:00 tea; 10:40 wee, small…

tools.prompt: Analyse this bladder diary: {diary} for the profile. Sections: kv (daily fluid total, number of voids, voids per night, longest gap, urgency episodes, estimated bladder capacity trend), a table (Pattern | Evidence | Likely driver | Fix), steps for a bladder-training plan with target gaps for the next 2 weeks, bullets on drink timing and irritants, and a callout on when to see a doctor (blood in urine, pain, sudden change, UTI signs).

tools.title: Diastasis check
tools.subtitle: Self-check + deep-core rehab

inputs.label: Your self-check
inputs.placeholder: 2 fingers wide above navel, feels soft, doming when I sit up

inputs.label: Photo of your belly during a gentle head lift (optional)

tools.prompt: Interpret the self-check: {finding} (and the photo if provided) for the profile. Sections: steps for a correct self-check to confirm (position, where to press, what to note: width, depth, tension), a callout with the likely category (functional gap vs needs assessment) and why tension matters more than width, a table (Week | Exercise | Sets × reps | Cue) for a 4-week deep-core progression, and bullets of movements to modify for now (and how) rather than avoid forever.

tools.title: Can I do this?
tools.subtitle: Exercise, lifting, running with symptoms

inputs.label: Activity
inputs.placeholder: return to running, CrossFit, carrying a toddler upstairs

tools.prompt: Assess {activity} for the profile's stage and issues. Sections: a callout with a verdict (Go / Modify / Not yet, build to it), a table (Version | Modification | Why | Progress when…), a checklist of readiness tests (e.g. for running: single-leg hop, 30 jumps, no leaking or heaviness), and bullets on breathing and pressure management during lifts.

tools.title: Pelvic physio visit
tools.subtitle: What happens, what to ask

inputs.label: Your story in a few lines
inputs.placeholder: leaking since second baby 2 years ago, worse on the trampoline, avoid running

tools.prompt: Prepare for a pelvic health physiotherapy appointment with: {story}. Sections: text on what a first assessment usually involves (history, external and, with consent, internal exam, what you can decline), bullets of 8 questions to ask, a checklist of what to track for a week beforehand, a quote with a one-line summary to open the appointment, and a callout on how to find a qualified pelvic physio and what a GP referral needs.

disclaimer: General pelvic health information, not medical advice or a substitute for assessment by a pelvic health physiotherapist or doctor. Seek care for pain, bleeding, blood in urine, or sudden changes.
